summary: Setup is hard: you can connect your own account within about an hour, but public launch needs Google verification. Restricted Gmail scopes (read, modify, compose) are the main thing that can hold up launch, because apps that access data through a server also need an annual third-party security assessment.
timeToProduction: ~2–3 weeks with gmail.send only; ~6+ weeks with restricted scopes
effort: 1–2 days of work, plus a demo video and privacy policy for review
cost: Free from Google; restricted scopes with server-side data need a paid third-party security assessment (cost agreed with the assessor)
handoff: An agent can pick the scopes and write the homepage, privacy policy and demo video script; you sign in to the Google Cloud console, create the project and client, copy the secret, connect a test account, record the video and submit for verification.

gates.title: Any Google account can register the app
Testing mode: up to 100 listed test users, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days
gates.what: While publishing status is Testing, only added test users can use the app and refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
gates.where: Google Auth platform → Audience in the Google Cloud console
gates.todo: Add your own account as a test user for development, then publish to production before real users connect.

gates.title: Google must verify the app before the general public can use sensitive or restricted scopes
gates.what: Public apps using sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes need verification. Brand verification takes 2–3 business days, sensitive scopes about 10 business days, restricted scopes about 6 weeks. Unverified apps hit a 100-user cap.
gates.where: Google Auth platform → Branding, Data Access and Verification Center in the Google Cloud console
gates.todo: Prefer gmail.send or non-sensitive scopes; otherwise prepare a homepage, privacy policy, scope justification and demo video and submit.

gates.title: Google Workspace admins can block or restrict the app
gates.what: If a Workspace admin restricts Gmail, users cannot add an app that requests a restricted service until the admin trusts it.
gates.where: Admin console → Security → Access and data control → API controls (the user's organization admin)
gates.todo: Give admins your OAuth client ID so they can trust it, and get the app verified.

gates.title: No paid API tier is mentioned
Annual reverification and security assessment for restricted scopes
gates.what: Apps with restricted scopes must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months to keep access.

requirements.text: A publicly accessible app homepage and a privacy policy on the same domain
A domain you own, verified in Google Search Console, for the authorized domains

steps.text: Your app: decide which Gmail scopes you need. This decides how much review Google requires.
steps.why: Restricted scopes trigger the longest review and a security assessment.
steps.detail: Send only: gmail.send (sensitive: verification). Read or change mail: gmail.readonly, gmail.compose or gmail.modify (restricted: verification, plus a security assessment if the data reaches your servers).

steps.text: Google Cloud console: select or create a project to hold the app.
steps.detail: Create it inside an organization if you use Google Workspace.

steps.text: APIs & Services → Library: search for Gmail API and click Enable.
steps.detail: Scopes can only be chosen after the API is enabled.

steps.text: Google Auth platform → Branding: click Get Started, enter the app name and user support email, choose External under Audience, add a contact email, agree to the user data policy and click Create.
Google Auth platform → Data Access: click Add or Remove Scopes, select the chosen Gmail scopes and click Save.
steps.detail: Scopes are grouped as non-sensitive, sensitive and restricted.

steps.text: APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID: choose Web application and add your callback URL as an authorized redirect URI.
steps.detail: Add your authorized domain first before adding redirect or policy URLs.

steps.text: Credentials → your OAuth client: click Create and copy the client ID and client secret.
steps.detail: Up to two secrets can exist at once for rotation.

steps.text: Google Auth platform → Audience → Test users: click Add users, enter your own email and other testers, then Save.
Browser: open Google's OAuth authorize URL built from your client ID, scopes and redirect URI, and sign in as a test user to approve access.
steps.detail: Template: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&scope=SCOPES&access_type=offline. Expect a tester warning screen.

steps.text: Your site: write the public homepage, a privacy policy on the same domain (with the Limited Use disclosure), and the demo video script showing the consent flow and each scope in use.
YouTube: record the demo video and upload it as Unlisted.
steps.why: Google's reviewers watch it to check how your app uses each scope you request.
steps.detail: Show the consent flow, your OAuth client ID in the address bar, and the feature each scope enables. You'll paste the link in step 14.

steps.text: Google Auth platform → Audience: click Publish app to move from Testing to In production.
steps.detail: Until Google verifies the app, users see an unverified-app warning and the project is capped at 100 new users.

steps.text: Google Auth platform → Branding: click Verify Branding, then Publish branding once it passes.
steps.detail: Publish within 7 days of a passing brand check or run it again.

steps.text: Verification Center: submit the data access request with your scope justification and demo video link.
steps.detail: Paste the YouTube link from step 11 in the YouTube link field.

steps.text: Verification Center: wait for Google's verification and respond to emails from the verification team.
steps.detail: Google estimates about 10 business days for sensitive scopes and 6 weeks for restricted scopes; not guaranteed.

steps.text: Google-approved assessor: if you use restricted scopes and store or transmit data on servers, hire an assessor to complete the security assessment.

blockers.problem: Users see the unverified app screen or Google sign-in is disabled after about 100 new users.
blockers.fix: Submit the app for verification before requesting sensitive or restricted scopes widely, and only call scopes you declared and got approved.

blockers.problem: Refresh tokens stop working after 7 days.
blockers.fix: The project is in Testing status; publish the consent screen to production.

blockers.problem: Using SMTP with the https://mail.google.com/ scope violates the minimum scope policy.
blockers.fix: Use the Gmail API with gmail.send instead.

blockers.problem: A Workspace admin has restricted Gmail, so users in that organization cannot add the app.
blockers.fix: Give admins your OAuth client ID so they can trust it.

claims.statement: Public apps that use sensitive or restricted scopes must complete verification unless they qualify for an exception.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: If your app requests sensitive or restricted scopes, you need to complete the verification process unless your app's use qualifies for an exception .

claims.statement: Brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days and must be done first.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Note that all apps must complete the brand verification step first, which typically takes 2-3 business days, if branding information has changed since the last approved OAuth consent screen verification.
claims.note: [Check: the quote only partly supports this. Quote says brand verification must be completed first and typically takes 2-3 business days, but it applies only if branding information has changed since last approval; the statement omits this condition.]

claims.statement: Google estimates 10 business days for sensitive scope verification and 6 weeks for restricted scope verification, not guaranteed.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Sensitive Scope Verification Ensure that an app’s usage of sensitive scopes is not deceptive and in alignment with the appropriate use case, limited use, and minimum scope requirements, to protect user data per the Google API policy and the Additional Requirements for Specific API Scopes . 10 Business days … An additional Security assessment is required to demonstrate a minimum level of capability in handling data securely and deleting user data upon user request. 6 weeks * Please note that these estimates are not guaranteed and will vary based on developer responsiveness
claims.note: Quoted from the table of verification types and times. Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Restricted scope verification involves a security assessment for apps that access data via a server and can take several weeks.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: One of these additional requirements occurs if the app accesses or has the capability to access Google user data from or through a server. In these cases, the system must undergo an annual security assessment from an independent, third-party assessor that is approved by Google. For this reason, the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: No special account, paid plan or approval for registering is mentioned in the OAuth client setup page.
claims.sourceTitle: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes
claims.note: No such requirement is mentioned in the OAuth consent setup page, where it would appear.

claims.statement: In Testing status the app is available only to listed test users.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: This setting means that your app is still in development and is only available to users you add to the list of test users.

claims.statement: External apps in Testing get refresh tokens expiring in 7 days (unless only basic profile scopes).
claims.sourceTitle: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs
claims.quote: A Google Cloud Platform project with an OAuth consent screen configured for an external user type and a publishing status of "Testing" is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days, unless the only OAuth scopes requested are a subset of name, email address, and user profile (through the userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, openid scopes, or their OpenID Connect equivalents ).

claims.statement: Unverified apps accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: To protect users and Google systems from abuse, unverified apps that are accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap restriction.

claims.statement: If Gmail access is restricted and an app requests a restricted service without being trusted, users can't add it.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data
claims.quote: While users are prompted to consent to apps, if an app requests access to a restricted service and you haven't specifically trusted the app, users can't add it.

claims.statement: Admins can mark apps Trusted, Limited or Blocked in API controls; Workspace admins can use a client ID given in help docs.
claims.sourceTitle: Additional considerations for Google Workspace
claims.quote: Google Workspace admins can give your app's OAuth client IDs access to restricted services and the high-risk scopes within.
claims.note: [Check: the quote only partly supports this. Quote only says Workspace admins can give OAuth client IDs access to restricted services; it does not mention Trusted, Limited or Blocked marks, API controls, or a client ID in help docs.]

claims.statement: No paid API tier is mentioned in the Gmail scopes page.
claims.sourceTitle: Choose Gmail API scopes
claims.note: No paid plan or API tier is mentioned in the Gmail scopes page.

claims.statement: Apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months to keep restricted scope access.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: As mentioned previously, to keep access to any verified restricted scopes, apps must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.

claims.statement: Home page must be public and the privacy policy hosted on the same domain.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users. … The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Ownership of authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console .

claims.statement: gmail.send is listed under sensitive scopes.
claims.sourceTitle: Choose Gmail API scopes
claims.quote: Sensitive scopes Scope code Description https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.addons.current.message.metadata View your email message metadata when the add-on is running. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.addons.current.message.readonly View your email messages when the add-on is running. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send Send email on your behalf. Restricted scopes
claims.note: Quoted from the scopes table, including its section headings. Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: gmail.readonly, gmail.compose and gmail.modify are listed under restricted scopes.
claims.sourceTitle: Choose Gmail API scopes
claims.quote: Restricted scopes Scope code Description https://mail.google.com/ Read, compose, send, and permanently delete all your email from Gmail. Note: Request this scope only if your application needs to immediately and permanently delete threads and messages, bypassing the trash. You can perform all other actions using less permissive scopes. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly View your email messages and settings. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.compose Manage drafts and send emails. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.insert Add emails into your Gmail mailbox. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.
claims.note: Quoted from the scopes table, starting at its Restricted scopes heading. Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Google recommends creating the project in an organization if using Workspace.
claims.sourceTitle: Additional considerations for Google Workspace
claims.quote: If you are a Google Workspace user, it is strongly recommended that your developer project is created inside a organization resource within your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity account.

claims.statement: The API must be enabled in the API Library to select its scopes.
claims.sourceTitle: Setting up OAuth 2.0 - API Console Help
claims.quote: To select scopes for registration, you need to enable the API, like Drive or Gmail, from APIs & Services > API Library.
claims.note: Page is marked outdated; menu path is consistent with the console.

claims.statement: With External user type, add test users under Audience → Test users → Add users, then Save.
claims.sourceTitle: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes
claims.quote: If you selected External for user type, add test users: Click Audience . Under Test users , click Add users . Enter your email address and any other authorized test users, then click Save .
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Scopes are added under Data Access > Add or Remove Scopes and saved.
claims.sourceTitle: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes
claims.quote: If you're creating an app for use outside of your Google Workspace organization, click Data Access > Add or Remove Scopes . … After selecting the scopes required by your app, click Save .
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Server-side apps must specify authorized redirect URIs.
claims.sourceTitle: Setting up OAuth 2.0 - API Console Help
claims.quote: Applications that access Google APIs from a server (often using languages and frameworks like Node.js, Java, .NET, and Python) must specify authorized redirect URIs .
claims.note: Page is marked outdated.

claims.statement: Add authorized domains before redirect URIs and policy URLs.
claims.sourceTitle: Setting up OAuth 2.0 - API Console Help
claims.quote: Add your Authorized Domains before you add your redirect or origin URIs, your homepage URL, your terms of service URL, or your privacy policy URL.
claims.note: Page is marked outdated.

claims.statement: A client can have at most two client secrets.
claims.sourceTitle: Setting up OAuth 2.0 - API Console Help
claims.quote: You can only have two client secrets at maximum.
claims.note: Page is marked outdated.

claims.statement: Unverified apps show an unverified app/tester warning screen.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Note: Your app is still subject to a tester warning screen, as shown in figure 1, a user cap is in effect, and the refresh token lifetime is limited.
claims.note: [Check: the quote only partly supports this. Quote says the app is subject to a tester warning screen, but does not mention an unverified app warning screen; it mentions user cap and refresh token limits instead.]

claims.statement: The demo video must be on YouTube as Unlisted and show the OAuth client ID in the address bar.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set Visibility as Unlisted . … Show that the browser address bar of the OAuth consent screen correctly includes your app's OAuth client ID.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Compliant brand verification results are valid for 7 days before publishing.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Note: Compliant verification results are valid for 7 days. If you don't publish within that timeframe, the status will change to Need to re-verify and you will have to run the brand verification again.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: The assessment cost is agreed between the developer and the assessor, without Google's involvement.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment. … The cost for such a service is agreed on between the developer and the assessor without any involvement from Google.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Approved apps requesting scopes they were not approved for see the unverified app screen.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: This is caused by approved apps making requests to sensitive or restricted scopes that the app has not been approved for during the verification process.

claims.statement: Refresh tokens can stop working after 6 months of non-use or a password change with Gmail scopes.
claims.sourceTitle: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs
claims.quote: The refresh token has not been used for six months. The user changed passwords and the refresh token contains Gmail scopes.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: SMTP-only use of the mail.google.com scope violates minimum scope policy; use gmail.send instead.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: If your app uses SMTP protocol only, note that using the broad access https://mail.google.com/ scope just for sending emails with the SMTP protocol violates the minimum scope policy . To use the Gmail API and continue with the verification process, you will need to migrate off SMTP protocol and use the sensitive https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send scope instead.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Consent screen setup: Google Auth platform → Branding → Get Started, app name and user support email, user type under Audience, a contact email, agree to the User Data Policy, then Create.
claims.sourceTitle: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.
claims.quote: In the Google API Console, go to Menu menu > Google Auth platform > Branding . … If you see a message that says Google Auth platform not configured yet , click Get Started : Under App Information , in App name , enter an App name . In User support email , choose a support email address where users can contact you if they have questions about their consent. … Under Audience , select the user type for your app. Click Next . Under Contact Information , enter an Email address where you can be notified about any changes to your project. Click Next . Under Finish , review the Google API Services User Data Policy and if you agree, select I agree to the Google API Services: User Data Policy . Click Continue . Click Create .

claims.statement: In Testing, a project is limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.
claims.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

claims.statement: Selecting Publish app moves the project to In production, where any Google Account user can use it.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.
claims.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of In production are available to any user with a Google Account. A project's publishing status is considered In production after selecting the Publish app button.

claims.statement: The demo video shows how a user grants access to the requested scopes and how the app uses each granted sensitive or restricted scope; its link goes in the YouTube link field.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification
claims.quote: Prepare a video that fully demonstrates how a user initiates and grants access to the requested scopes and shows, in detail, the usage of the granted sensitive and restricted scopes in the app. Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set Visibility as Unlisted . You need to provide a link to the demonstration video in the YouTube link field.
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.
